doc: satpipe run configuration
Name of the run; used in the manifest and in output file names.
Run directory. Every stage writes to <out_dir>/<stage>/.
Species/assembly code -> genome FASTA. The code is used in every locus name (`code|scaffold:start-end`), so keep it short and free of `|`, `:` and `-`.
Pre-computed inputs that let a run start after a stage.
Code -> TRF `.dat` file for that genome. When given for every genome, stage 02 (TRF scan) is skipped. The published Darevskia run starts here.
Family -> seed BED6 (0-based). When given for every family, stages 03-10 are skipped and the run starts at expansion (stage 11).
One block per satellite family.
Single-record FASTA with one monomer of the family consensus.
Monomer length in bp. Drives every window size (3xMONO walk, 2xMONO scan window, D3 widths, viewer step). Should equal the consensus length; `satpipe check` warns if it does not.
Display colour for the viewer (hex). Optional.
Reference files that feed specific stages.

Phase-rotated family consensuses prepended in Step 8 (`CLsat_cons.rot` in the Darevskia run). Prepending makes each reference win centroid election for its family. If absent the driver derives it by applying the Step-5 rotation to each `families.*.consensus` and records that deviation in the manifest.
Stages 02-08: TRF scan, motif extraction, filtering, clustering.
TRF parameters: match mismatch delta PM PI minscore maxperiod.
Motif period range [min, max] accepted by Step 3.
Minimum TRF copy number for a motif (Step 3).

Step 3b: replace a motif that is k tandem copies of a shorter unit (TRF reporting an array at a multiple of its unit, e.g. 292 for a 146-letter unit) by one unit. Test: the motif against itself rotated by len/k, banded global alignment, identity >= monomer_min_id; units never shorter than period[0]. Added 2026-10-18; the published run had no such step (set false to reproduce it exactly).

Step 3b: minimum self-identity (motif vs itself rotated by one unit) to call a motif k units. Random and AT-rich random sequence of motif lengths stays far below (0 of 2 000 called in the 2026-10-18 test).
Step 4: motifs whose own TRF re-scan covers more than this many bp are dropped as simple repeats.
Step 5 canonical rotation and vsearch clustering strand. The published run is plus-only (deliberate; it is what left L541 unclustered).
vsearch identity for per-species clustering (Step 6).
vsearch identity for cross-species clustering (Step 8).

Curated TSV: `cluster<TAB>family[<TAB>note]`, cluster = vsearch cluster number from Step 8. Validated at stage 09: every listed cluster must exist, every family must have at least one cluster; unassigned clusters are reported with sizes and best-consensus bits for the curator.
Stage 11: seed expansion (`clisat_expand_then_scan_merged.sh`).
--min-bits: minimum ssearch36 bits to accept a window.
--min-aln-frac: fraction of the window (win_mono x MONO) that must align.
--step-monomers: dense-walk step, in monomers.
--win-monomers: probe window width, in monomers.
--query-repeat N: the ssearch36 query is N+1 tandem copies of the consensus.
--probe-monomers: coarse-probe initial step, in monomers.
--probe-min-step: coarse-probe minimum step, in monomers.
--max-steps: dense-walk cap per direction (0 = unlimited).
--to-scaffold-ends.
--jobs: GNU parallel workers.
Stage 13: symmetric rescan of MASTER loci with every family consensus.
Scan window width in monomers (--scan-win-bp = win_mono x MONO).
Scan step in monomers (--scan-step-bp = step_mono x MONO).
--scan-min-bits: minimum bits to emit a scan row.
Stage 14: segmentation and family arbitration.
DELTA: seed/rescan contradiction threshold (UNIQUE_SEED_CONTRADICTION at delta <= -DELTA).
DELTA_AMBIG: ambiguity flag threshold.
SEG_BIN: D3b bin width in bp.
SEG_MIN_RUN: minimum run of bins to start a segment.
SEG_MIN_LOCUS: segments shorter than this are handled per `short_segments`.
SEG_SHORT: `drop` is the published behaviour; `merge` folds short segments into the longer neighbour.

BIN_MIN_BITS: a 1-kb bin counts as satellite when its best window reaches this many bits (used by the bin-majority family rule). Absolute scores depend on the monomer length and the scoring, so set it per satellite. Default: expansion.min_bits.

MAX_GAP_MONO: a run of non-satellite 1-kb bins (best window under bin_min_bits) at least this long, in monomers x the longest family monomer, cuts a locus; the gap belongs to no locus. Shorter gaps stay inside the locus and are reported (gap_bins). 0 = never cut. Not in the published run (author's decision 2026-10-26: 100 monomers = 14.6 kb for CLsat).

BIN_SHARE: segments, seed conflicts and unseeded loci take the family that wins most 1-kb bins (bins whose best window reaches arbitration.bin_min_bits); the call is _AMBIGUOUS when that family holds less than this share of the bins. Not in the published run, which used the locus-wide maximum window (author's decision 2026-10-25).

Haplotype-duplicate rule at stage 16 (`hapdup_filter.sh`). Off unless `pairs` is given. In a trio-phased assembly reads without parent-specific k-mers go to both haplotypes, so a pure satellite array can be assembled twice. A contig whose catalogue loci cover all of it (array-only) is removed when it aligns (minimap2 asm5) over min_qcov of its length at gap-compressed identity >= min_ident to the partner haplotype, with >= min_tovl of the hit inside partner loci on contigs that are not array-only. Every array-only contig and its verdict is listed in regions/hapdup.tsv.
Pairs of genome codes that are the two haplotype copies of one animal, e.g. [[unif, unim], [armf, armm]].
bp at each contig end that the loci may leave uncovered and still count as array-only.
Minimum share of the array-only contig covered by the hit.
Minimum gap-compressed identity (1 - minimap2 de) of the hit.
Minimum share of the partner stretch inside anchored partner loci.
Flank orthology (`rebuild_ortho_segmented.py`).
FLANK: flank length extracted outward from each array edge.
GUARD: extra distance a flank must keep from another locus.
Minimum aligned length for an ortholog hit.
Minimum percent identity for an ortholog hit.
Sub-subfamily assignment at array boundaries.
Directory of per-sub-subfamily consensus FASTA files (`subx/` in the Darevskia run) or one multi-record FASTA. Optional: without it the stage is skipped.
Family -> list of its sub-subfamily names (the FAMSUBS table). Each family listed must exist in `families`.
Bits margin over the second-best sub-subfamily for a confident call.
Terminal-monomer and boundary-phase measurement.
Window into the array from each terminus, in monomers.
EDGE_TOL: tolerated gap between alignment and array edge, bp.
Optional finalisation stages (large-scaffold recovery, edge refinement, re-arbitration).
Scaffolds longer than this are TRF-scanned in overlapping chunks (the published run needed this for one 85.8 Mb unp scaffold).
Chunk size for the chunked TRF scan.
Chunk overlap for the chunked TRF scan.
Seconds after which a chunk's TRF run is stopped and the chunk bisected (the published run's chunk 44 of the 85 Mb scaffold never finished: a telomeric tail).
Pieces shorter than this are no longer bisected; if TRF still times out on them they are listed in unscanned.tsv and left out (never imputed).
EDGE_TOL used by edge refinement.
No effect (kept so old configs load): stage 14 always arbitrates the final catalogue; there is no separate re-arbitration pass.
Anchor phasing (stage 21): every consensus the run writes is rotated into the frame of the anchor family, so figures, alignments and deposited FASTA share one start.
Family whose consensus defines the frame. Default: the first family under `families`.
Motif the anchor frame must start with (Darevskia CLsat: AAAGAAG). Empty: the anchor family's consensus is used exactly as given.

Families are unrelated (no common frame exists, e.g. different satellites of one genome): each family consensus is its own frame and only sub-subfamilies are rotated, onto their family. Default false: all families must be placeable on the anchor.
Mismatches tolerated between the motif and the start of a rotated sequence (diverged families, e.g. CLsat4, may differ by one base).
Minimum identity of the local alignment to the anchor for a sequence to be placed; below it the stage fails instead of guessing a frame.

Optional BED of hand-added loci (L541 in the Darevskia catalogue): chrom start end `<genome>|...` [score strand family]; col 4 must start with a genome code, col 7 (optional) names the family, else the best-scoring family is used. Entries are tagged MANUAL in provenance and listed in the manifest.
Optional executable overrides: tool name -> path. The special key `bin_dir` is a directory searched before PATH for every tool.
Viewer configuration written by `satpipe viewer`.
Page title.
Code -> display name. Keys must exist in `genomes`.
